Software Developer.description: Design, build, and maintain software applications across platforms.

Programming Fundamentals.reason: Core programming concepts like variables, loops, functions, and OOP are the foundation every software developer builds upon regardless of language or domain.

Data Structures & Algorithms.reason: DSA is tested in every technical interview and is essential for writing efficient, scalable software. Without it, you cannot pass hiring assessments at top companies.

Git & Version Control.reason: Git is used by every professional software team. Without it, you cannot collaborate on code, track changes, or contribute to any real-world project.

Object-Oriented Programming.reason: OOP principles (classes, inheritance, encapsulation, polymorphism) are the foundation of most large-scale software systems and frameworks.

Databases.reason: Almost every application stores and retrieves data. Understanding SQL and basic database design is a must-have skill for any developer.

Software Design Patterns.reason: Design patterns are reusable solutions to common software problems. They help you write maintainable, scalable code and communicate better with your team.

Testing & Debugging.reason: Writing unit tests and debugging skills separate junior developers from seniors. Professional codebases require tested, reliable code.

Software Engineer.description: Apply engineering principles to design robust, scalable software systems.

Data Structures & Algorithms.reason: Software engineering interviews at top companies are DSA-heavy. Beyond interviews, efficient algorithms are essential for systems that scale to millions of users.

System Design.reason: Software engineers are expected to design large-scale distributed systems. System design skills differentiate mid-level from senior engineers.

Programming (Python/Java/C++).reason: Deep proficiency in at least one language is required. Software engineers must write production-quality, performant code, not just working code.

Operating Systems.reason: Understanding processes, threads, memory management, and file systems is essential for writing performant software and debugging hard issues.

Networking Fundamentals.reason: Modern software runs over networks. Understanding TCP/IP, HTTP, DNS, and sockets is required for building distributed systems and APIs.

Databases & SQL.reason: Every software system persists data. Deep knowledge of relational databases, indexing, and query optimization is core to engineering roles.

Cloud & Deployment.reason: Modern software is deployed to cloud infrastructure. Understanding AWS/GCP/Azure, containers, and CI/CD pipelines is increasingly expected.

Backend Developer.description: Build and maintain server-side logic, APIs, and database systems.

Server-Side Language (Python/Node/Java).reason: Backend development requires deep proficiency in a server-side language. Python (Django/Flask), Node.js (Express), or Java (Spring) are the most in-demand.

REST API Design.reason: Backend developers spend most of their time building and maintaining REST APIs. Understanding HTTP methods, status codes, and API design best practices is essential.

Databases & SQL.reason: The backend is the bridge between the application and the database. Deep SQL knowledge and database design skills are non-negotiable.

Authentication & Security.reason: Backend developers are responsible for securing APIs with JWT, OAuth, password hashing, and preventing SQL injection and XSS attacks.

Caching (Redis).reason: Caching with Redis dramatically improves application performance by reducing database load. It is a standard tool in production backend systems.

Message Queues.reason: RabbitMQ, Kafka, and Celery are used for async task processing and decoupling services in scalable backend architectures.

Docker & Deployment.reason: Backend services are containerized and deployed via Docker. Understanding containers and basic CI/CD is expected in modern backend roles.

Frontend Developer.description: Build beautiful, responsive user interfaces and web experiences.

HTML.reason: HTML is the skeleton of every web page. Semantic HTML is critical for accessibility, SEO, and building well-structured interfaces.

CSS.reason: CSS controls all visual presentation. Mastery of Flexbox, Grid, animations, and responsive design is the core skill of frontend development.

JavaScript.reason: JavaScript is the only language that runs natively in browsers. Deep JS knowledge including DOM, events, async, and closures is the foundation of all frontend work.

React or Vue.reason: Modern frontend development is component-based. React is the most in-demand framework and virtually every frontend job listing requires it.

TypeScript.reason: TypeScript is now standard in professional frontend codebases. It catches bugs at compile time and makes large codebases maintainable.

CSS Frameworks (Tailwind).reason: Tailwind CSS is the most popular utility-first CSS framework, dramatically speeding up UI development and used widely in production apps.

Web Performance.reason: Optimizing load times, Core Web Vitals, and rendering performance directly impacts user experience and SEO rankings.

Full Stack Developer.description: Build complete web applications handling both frontend and backend.

HTML, CSS & JavaScript.reason: Full stack development starts with solid frontend fundamentals. You cannot build complete web apps without mastering the core web technologies.

React (Frontend Framework).reason: React is the most widely used frontend framework. Full stack developers are expected to build dynamic UIs with React in most modern web stacks.

Node.js & Express.reason: Node.js allows JavaScript on the backend, enabling true full stack development in one language. Express is the most popular Node.js framework.

Databases (SQL & NoSQL).reason: Full stack developers must handle data storage on both relational (PostgreSQL) and NoSQL (MongoDB) databases depending on project needs.

REST APIs & GraphQL.reason: Full stack developers build the APIs their own frontends consume. REST and GraphQL are the two dominant API paradigms in modern web development.

Git & Deployment.reason: Full stack developers are expected to deploy their own apps. Git for version control and platforms like Vercel or AWS for deployment are essential.

Docker & CI/CD.reason: Containerizing full stack apps with Docker and automating deployments with CI/CD pipelines is the professional standard for shipping software.

Application Developer.description: Build desktop and cross-platform applications for end users.

Programming Language (Python/Java/C#).reason: Application development requires strong proficiency in a language suited to the target platform. Python for tools, Java for cross-platform, C# for Windows.

GUI Frameworks.reason: Desktop apps require GUI frameworks like Tkinter, JavaFX, or Electron to build user interfaces that run outside the browser.

Object-Oriented Programming.reason: Application development is heavily OOP-based. Classes, inheritance, and design patterns are central to building maintainable desktop software.

File I/O & Data Storage.reason: Applications need to read and write files, manage local storage, and often use embedded databases like SQLite for persistence.

Software Testing.reason: Application bugs affect end users directly. Unit testing, integration testing, and UI testing ensure application reliability.

Packaging & Distribution.reason: Shipping desktop apps requires packaging them into installers using PyInstaller, NSIS, or MSI. Understanding app distribution pipelines is essential.

Web Developer.description: Build responsive, interactive websites and web applications.

HTML.reason: HTML is the skeleton of every web page. Without it, no web content can be structured or displayed in a browser.

CSS.reason: CSS controls visual presentation. Modern CSS with Flexbox and Grid is essential for responsive, beautiful layouts.

JavaScript.reason: JavaScript is the only language that runs natively in browsers, making it essential for interactive web experiences.

React.reason: React is the most in-demand frontend framework. It enables building reusable UI components and managing complex app state.

Git.reason: Version control with Git is non-negotiable in professional development. Every team uses it for collaboration and code management.

Node.js.reason: Node.js allows JavaScript on the server side, enabling full-stack development with a single language.

Databases.reason: Web apps need to store and retrieve data. Understanding SQL (PostgreSQL) and NoSQL (MongoDB) databases is essential.

TypeScript.reason: TypeScript adds static typing to JavaScript, reducing bugs and improving code maintainability in large codebases.

Mobile App Developer.description: Build native and cross-platform mobile applications for iOS and Android.

JavaScript.reason: JavaScript powers React Native, the most popular cross-platform mobile framework, enabling one codebase for iOS and Android.

React Native.reason: React Native lets you build truly native mobile apps with JavaScript, dramatically reducing development time vs building separate iOS/Android apps.

Mobile UI/UX Design.reason: Mobile interfaces have unique constraints including touch targets, screen sizes, and gestures. Understanding platform-specific design guidelines is essential.

REST APIs.reason: Mobile apps rarely work in isolation. They consume REST APIs to fetch data, authenticate users, and sync information.

App Store Deployment.reason: Understanding the App Store and Google Play submission processes, certificates, and policies is required to ship apps to users.

Swift or Kotlin.reason: Native languages deliver the best performance and deepest platform integration for complex mobile apps requiring platform-specific features.

Game Developer.description: Design and build interactive video games for PC, console, or mobile.

C# or C++.reason: C# is the primary language for Unity (the most popular game engine), and C++ is used in Unreal Engine. One of these is required for professional game development.

Game Engine (Unity/Unreal).reason: Modern games are built in game engines. Unity dominates mobile and indie games while Unreal dominates AAA. Deep engine knowledge is the core skill.

Linear Algebra & Math.reason: Game development relies heavily on vectors, matrices, and trigonometry for 3D transformations, physics, camera systems, and collision detection.

Game Physics.reason: Realistic movement, collision, gravity, and rigid body dynamics require understanding of game physics systems like PhysX and Box2D.

3D Modeling Basics.reason: Game developers need to understand 3D asset pipelines including meshes, textures, and UV mapping even if they do not create all assets themselves.

Shader Programming.reason: Custom shaders written in HLSL/GLSL control how surfaces are rendered and are essential for achieving high-quality visual effects.

Data Scientist.description: Analyze complex data to extract insights and build predictive models.

Python.reason: Python is the primary language for data science. Libraries like pandas, NumPy, and scikit-learn are Python-native and used in virtually every data science workflow.
resources: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python

Statistics.reason: Statistical thinking is foundational to data science, from hypothesis testing to understanding model performance metrics.

Machine Learning.reason: Machine learning is the core skill of data science, building models that learn patterns from data to make predictions.

SQL.reason: Most real-world data lives in relational databases. SQL is essential for extracting, filtering, and aggregating data before analysis.

Data Visualization.reason: Communicating findings visually is key. Tools like Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Tableau help turn numbers into actionable insights.

Pandas & NumPy.reason: Pandas and NumPy are the go-to libraries for data manipulation and numerical computing in Python, used in every data science project.

Deep Learning.reason: Deep learning enables complex tasks like image recognition and NLP. It is increasingly expected for senior data science roles.

Machine Learning Engineer.description: Build, train, and deploy machine learning models at production scale.

Python.reason: Python is the dominant language for ML engineering. PyTorch, TensorFlow, and scikit-learn are all Python-first frameworks.

Machine Learning Algorithms.reason: Deep understanding of supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning algorithms is the core knowledge of an ML engineer.

Deep Learning & Neural Networks.reason: Neural networks including CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers power modern ML systems. PyTorch or TensorFlow proficiency is required.

MLOps & Model Deployment.reason: ML engineers are responsible for deploying models to production using tools like MLflow, Docker, and REST APIs, not just training models in notebooks.

Feature Engineering.reason: The quality of features fed into a model often matters more than the algorithm. Feature engineering is the most impactful skill for improving model accuracy.

Mathematics (Linear Algebra, Calculus).reason: Understanding gradient descent, backpropagation, and matrix operations requires linear algebra and calculus knowledge.

Cloud ML Platforms.reason: Production ML runs on cloud platforms. AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, and Azure ML are used for training and serving models at scale.

AI Engineer.description: Design, build, and deploy AI systems and intelligent applications.

Python.reason: Python is the dominant language in AI/ML. Virtually all AI frameworks including TensorFlow, PyTorch, and LangChain are Python-first.

Machine Learning.reason: Understanding ML fundamentals is the foundation everything else in AI engineering builds upon.

Deep Learning.reason: Modern AI is built on deep learning. Neural networks, transformers, and CNNs are now core engineering knowledge.

Large Language Models.reason: LLMs are transforming the industry. AI Engineers must know how to fine-tune, prompt engineer, and deploy them using LangChain or similar tools.

MLOps.reason: Deploying AI models to production requires MLOps including CI/CD for ML, model monitoring, versioning, and serving infrastructure.

Cloud Platforms.reason: AI at scale requires cloud infrastructure. AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, and Azure ML are where production AI lives.

Mathematics.reason: Linear algebra, calculus, and probability theory underpin all AI algorithms.

NLP Engineer.description: Build systems that understand, process, and generate human language.

Python.reason: Python is the standard language for NLP. All major NLP libraries including NLTK, spaCy, and Hugging Face Transformers are Python-native.

Linguistics & Text Processing.reason: Understanding tokenization, stemming, lemmatization, POS tagging, and syntactic parsing is the foundation of all NLP work.

Transformer Models (BERT, GPT).reason: Transformers are the dominant architecture in modern NLP. BERT for understanding tasks and GPT for generation are used in virtually every production NLP system.

Machine Learning.reason: NLP models are ML models. Understanding classification, sequence labeling, and generative modeling is required for NLP engineering.

Deep Learning (PyTorch/TensorFlow).reason: Modern NLP uses neural networks. PyTorch is the preferred framework for NLP research and production systems.

Vector Databases & Embeddings.reason: Semantic search, RAG systems, and recommendation engines use text embeddings stored in vector databases like Pinecone and Weaviate.

LLM Fine-tuning & Prompt Engineering.reason: Production NLP systems now involve fine-tuning LLMs on domain data and advanced prompt engineering for optimal outputs.

Computer Vision Engineer.description: Build systems that analyze, understand, and process visual data.

Python.reason: Python is the primary language for computer vision. OpenCV, PyTorch, and TensorFlow, the core CV tools, are all Python-native.

Deep Learning (CNNs).reason: Convolutional Neural Networks are the backbone of modern computer vision. Image classification, detection, and segmentation all use CNNs.

OpenCV.reason: OpenCV is the most widely used computer vision library. It is used for image preprocessing, feature detection, and real-time video processing.

Object Detection Frameworks.reason: YOLO, Faster R-CNN, and DETR are industry-standard object detection frameworks used in robotics, surveillance, and autonomous systems.

Image Segmentation.reason: Semantic and instance segmentation is essential for medical imaging, autonomous driving, and industrial computer vision applications.

Mathematics (Linear Algebra).reason: Image transformations, convolutions, and 3D geometry rely on linear algebra. It is required to understand how CV algorithms work.

Edge Deployment (TensorRT/ONNX).reason: CV models deployed on cameras, robots, and mobile devices require model optimization with TensorRT or ONNX for real-time inference.

DevOps Engineer.description: Automate and streamline software delivery, infrastructure, and operations.

Linux & Shell Scripting.reason: DevOps engineers manage Linux servers and automate tasks with Bash scripts. Linux proficiency is the most fundamental skill in DevOps.

Docker & Containers.reason: Containerization with Docker is the foundation of modern DevOps. Every application is containerized for consistency across environments.

Kubernetes.reason: Kubernetes is the industry standard for orchestrating containers at scale. It is required for virtually every senior DevOps role.

CI/CD Pipelines.reason: DevOps engineers design and maintain CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or GitLab CI to automate testing and deployment.

Infrastructure as Code (Terraform).reason: IaC tools like Terraform allow infrastructure to be version-controlled and reproducible, a key DevOps principle.

Cloud Platforms (AWS/GCP/Azure).reason: DevOps engineers manage cloud infrastructure. AWS is the most in-demand, but knowledge of any major cloud platform is essential.

Monitoring & Observability.reason: Production systems require monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana, and ELK stack to detect issues before they impact users.

Cloud Engineer.description: Design and manage scalable cloud infrastructure and services.

Cloud Platforms (AWS/GCP/Azure).reason: Cloud engineers live and breathe cloud platforms. Deep knowledge of at least one major cloud provider is the core requirement for this role.

Networking (VPC, DNS, Load Balancing).reason: Cloud infrastructure is fundamentally network-based. Understanding VPCs, subnets, security groups, and load balancers is essential.

Infrastructure as Code (Terraform/CDK).reason: Cloud engineers provision infrastructure programmatically using Terraform or AWS CDK, not manually through consoles.

Linux & Scripting.reason: Cloud instances run Linux. Shell scripting and Linux administration are needed for automation and server management.

Containers & Kubernetes.reason: Modern cloud workloads run in containers. EKS, GKE, and AKS are managed Kubernetes services used on every major cloud platform.

Cloud Security.reason: IAM, encryption, security groups, and compliance frameworks like SOC2 and HIPAA are critical responsibilities of cloud engineers.

Cost Optimization.reason: Cloud costs can spiral out of control. Cloud engineers optimize spending using reserved instances, auto-scaling, and right-sizing.

Site Reliability Engineer.description: Ensure system reliability, scalability, and performance at production scale.

Linux & Systems Administration.reason: SREs manage complex production Linux systems. Deep OS-level knowledge of processes, memory, file systems, and networking is foundational.
resources: UNIX and Linux System Administration Handbook

Programming (Python/Go).reason: SREs write automation, tooling, and services. Python and Go are the dominant languages, Go for performance and Python for scripting.

Monitoring & Observability.reason: SREs define SLIs and SLOs and monitor them. Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, and distributed tracing are core SRE tools.

Incident Management.reason: SREs own production incidents. Understanding incident response, postmortems, and on-call management is central to the SRE role.

Kubernetes & Cloud.reason: Production systems run on cloud infrastructure. SREs manage Kubernetes clusters, auto-scaling, and cloud resources for reliability.

Chaos Engineering.reason: SREs proactively test system resilience using chaos engineering, intentionally injecting failures to find weaknesses before they cause outages.

Embedded Systems Developer.description: Program microcontrollers and hardware systems with low-level code.

C & C++.reason: C is the primary language of embedded systems. Direct hardware access, memory management, and real-time constraints require C/C++, not higher-level languages.

Microcontroller Programming.reason: Embedded developers program microcontrollers like Arduino, STM32, and ESP32. Understanding registers, interrupts, and timers is essential.
resources: Embedded Systems Shape The World (UT Austin - free)

Electronics & Circuit Design.reason: Embedded developers interface software with hardware. Understanding circuits, GPIO, I2C, SPI, and UART protocols is fundamental.

Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS).reason: Many embedded systems require deterministic timing. FreeRTOS and Zephyr are used in safety-critical and real-time applications.

Debugging & Testing (JTAG/GDB).reason: Debugging embedded systems requires hardware debuggers (JTAG/SWD) and tools like GDB. Bugs in embedded systems can cause physical failures.

Linux Kernel & Device Drivers.reason: Embedded Linux requires knowledge of kernel modules, device trees, and writing Linux device drivers for platforms like Raspberry Pi and Yocto.

Cybersecurity Engineer.description: Protect systems and networks from digital threats and attacks.

Networking Fundamentals.reason: Understanding TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, and network protocols is the foundation of cybersecurity because attacks happen over networks.

Linux.reason: Most servers and security tools run on Linux. Command-line proficiency and system administration are essential.

Python.reason: Python is used for scripting security tools, automating tasks, building exploits, and parsing logs in security workflows.

Ethical Hacking & Penetration Testing.reason: Penetration testing teaches you to think like an attacker, which is essential for identifying vulnerabilities before malicious actors do.

Cryptography.reason: Encryption, hashing, and PKI are the backbone of secure communications. You must understand how and why they work.

SIEM & Incident Response.reason: Security engineers use SIEM tools like Splunk and IBM QRadar for threat detection, log analysis, and incident response.

Cloud Security.reason: As organizations move to cloud, securing AWS/Azure/GCP environments is a rapidly growing and high-demand specialization.

Ethical Hacker.description: Legally test and break into systems to find vulnerabilities before attackers do.

Networking & Protocols.reason: Ethical hackers must deeply understand how networks work including TCP/IP, DNS, ARP, and HTTP to identify and exploit network-level vulnerabilities.

Linux & Command Line.reason: Ethical hacking tools like Kali Linux, Metasploit, and Nmap run on Linux. Deep CLI skills are non-negotiable.

Penetration Testing Methodology.reason: Ethical hackers follow structured methodologies like PTES and OWASP for reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation, and reporting.

Web Application Hacking.reason: Web apps are the most common attack surface. Understanding SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, and IDOR is required for any ethical hacking role.

Exploit Development.reason: Writing and modifying exploits requires understanding buffer overflows, shellcode, and memory corruption, the technical core of offensive security.

Scripting (Python/Bash).reason: Ethical hackers write custom scripts to automate reconnaissance, modify existing exploits, and process large amounts of output data.

Certifications (CEH/OSCP).reason: The OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional) is the gold standard ethical hacking certification and is required by many employers.

Software Tester / QA Automation Engineer.description: Ensure software quality through manual and automated testing strategies.

Testing Fundamentals.reason: Understanding the software testing lifecycle including unit, integration, system, and acceptance testing along with TDD and BDD methodologies is foundational.

Test Automation (Selenium/Playwright).reason: QA automation engineers write scripts to automate test cases. Selenium and Playwright are the most widely used UI automation frameworks.

Programming (Python/Java).reason: Writing automated test scripts requires programming skills. Python and Java are the most common languages used in QA automation frameworks.

API Testing.reason: Modern apps are API-driven. Testing APIs with Postman and REST Assured is a core QA skill alongside UI testing.

CI/CD Integration.reason: QA engineers integrate automated test suites into CI/CD pipelines so tests run automatically on every code change.

Performance Testing.reason: Load testing with JMeter or k6 ensures applications handle production traffic levels without degrading performance.

Test Management Tools.reason: Tools like Jira, TestRail, and Zephyr are used to plan, track, and report on test coverage and defect management in professional teams.

Blockchain Developer.description: Build decentralized applications and smart contracts on blockchain platforms.

Blockchain Fundamentals.reason: Understanding consensus mechanisms, distributed ledgers, cryptographic hashing, and the difference between blockchains is prerequisite knowledge.

Solidity & Smart Contracts.reason: Solidity is the primary language for writing Ethereum smart contracts. It is the core technical skill for most blockchain developer roles.

JavaScript/TypeScript.reason: Blockchain frontends and testing scripts are written in JS/TS. Libraries like Ethers.js and Web3.js are JavaScript-based.

Web3 Development (Ethers.js/Hardhat).reason: Web3 tooling connects frontend applications to the blockchain. Hardhat for testing/deployment and Ethers.js for interaction are industry standards.

DeFi & Tokenomics.reason: Understanding DeFi protocols, ERC standards (ERC-20, ERC-721), and tokenomics is essential for building real-world blockchain applications.

Cryptography.reason: Blockchain security relies on public-key cryptography, digital signatures, and hash functions. Understanding these is critical for secure contract development.

Smart Contract Security.reason: Smart contract bugs are irreversible and can result in millions lost. Auditing for reentrancy, overflow, and access control vulnerabilities is a senior skill.

AR/VR Developer.description: Build augmented and virtual reality experiences for headsets and mobile devices.

Unity or Unreal Engine.reason: Unity is the dominant platform for AR/VR development, supporting Meta Quest, HoloLens, and mobile AR. Unreal is used for high-fidelity VR experiences.

C# or C++.reason: Unity uses C# and Unreal uses C++. Proficiency in the scripting language of your chosen engine is required to build any AR/VR interaction.

3D Math & Spatial Computing.reason: AR/VR is entirely spatial. Quaternions, 3D transformations, raycasting, and coordinate spaces are core mathematical concepts for this field.

XR SDKs (OpenXR/ARKit/ARCore).reason: Cross-platform XR development uses OpenXR, ARKit (Apple), and ARCore (Google). These SDKs enable spatial tracking, hand tracking, and AR anchors.

3D Modeling & Asset Pipeline.reason: AR/VR developers need to understand how 3D assets are created, optimized, and imported, even if they do not create them.

UI/UX for Spatial Interfaces.reason: Designing interfaces in 3D space requires specialized UX thinking including diegetic UI, gaze interaction, and motion sickness prevention guidelines.

Performance Optimization.reason: VR requires 90+ FPS to prevent motion sickness. Occlusion culling, LODs, draw call batching, and shader optimization are essential for VR performance.

Robotics Programmer.description: Program robots and autonomous systems to perceive, decide, and act.

C++ & Python.reason: C++ is used for real-time, performance-critical robot control. Python is used for high-level logic, perception, and ROS 2 scripting. Both are essential.

ROS 2 (Robot Operating System).reason: ROS 2 is the standard middleware for robotics. It handles sensor data, inter-process communication, and robot simulation. Virtually every robotics job uses it.

Kinematics & Robot Control.reason: Programming robot motion requires understanding forward/inverse kinematics, PID controllers, and trajectory planning.

Sensor Integration (LIDAR, Camera, IMU).reason: Robots perceive their environment through sensors. Integrating and processing LIDAR point clouds, camera images, and IMU data is a core robotics skill.

SLAM & Navigation.reason: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping enables robots to navigate unknown environments. Nav2 in ROS 2 implements SLAM and path planning.

Simulation (Gazebo/Isaac Sim).reason: Testing robot software in simulation before deploying to hardware saves time and prevents damage. Gazebo and NVIDIA Isaac Sim are standard tools.

Machine Learning for Robotics.reason: Reinforcement learning and computer vision are increasingly used for robot manipulation, grasping, and autonomous decision-making.

Database Developer.description: Design, optimize, and manage databases that power applications and analytics.

SQL (Advanced).reason: Advanced SQL including window functions, CTEs, complex joins, subqueries, and stored procedures is the primary skill of a database developer.

Database Design & Normalization.reason: Designing efficient schemas with proper normalization, ER diagrams, and relationship design prevents data redundancy and ensures integrity.

PostgreSQL or MySQL.reason: Deep expertise in at least one major RDBMS including configuration, administration, and advanced features is the core database developer skill.

Query Optimization & Indexing.reason: Database performance is determined by query plans and indexes. Understanding EXPLAIN, index types, and query tuning is essential for production databases.

NoSQL Databases.reason: Different problems require different databases. MongoDB for documents, Redis for caching, Cassandra for time-series. Knowing when to use each is critical.

Database Administration.reason: Database developers need DBA skills including backups, replication, security, user management, and high availability configurations.

Data Warehousing & ETL.reason: Building data pipelines and warehouses with Snowflake, Redshift, or BigQuery using ETL processes is a specialized, high-demand database skill.
